explanation: Store every credit relative to one global offset. AddAll changes only the offset, while a sorted set of normalized credits identifies a maximum client. Replacing or removing a client updates both indexes.
timeComplexity: Insert/Remove/Max: O(log n); Lookup: O(1) expected; AddAll: O(1). The operation bounds reflect the displayed index: ordered set, randomized treap, or a Python scan for Max.
spaceComplexity: O(n). The client dictionary and any ranking index contain one entry per live client.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Each stored credit plus the common offset equals that client’s observable credit. AddAll preserves this invariant by changing only the offset. Insertion/removal updates both the client map and ordered ranking, so the highest ranked normalized credit also has the highest observable credit.
walkthrough: Insert client Nora with credit 4, then AddAll(6): Lookup(Nora) is 10. Reinsert Nora with credit 3, which replaces its absolute credit. Max is Nora; after removal Lookup is −1 and Max is empty. JSON arguments are [operations], with each operation [name,stringArg,intArg]. lookup/remove/max records carry expected observations, not extra callable parameters. Observed true means all operations validated.
edgeCases: Reinserting a client replaces its credit.
Missing removal returns false and missing lookup returns −1.
Initialize clears both indexes and resets the offset.
The judge maintains expected credits independently and accepts any existing client with the maximum credit. No universal tie-breaker is required.
